records.literal_gloss: Was now a man of the Pharisees, Nicodemus name to him, a ruler of the Jews;

en.L: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, Nicodemus [was] his name, a ruler of the Jews.

en.R: There was a man named Nicodemus. He was a Pharisee and one of the leaders of the Jewish people.

es.R: Había un hombre llamado Nicodemo. Era fariseo y uno de los dirigentes del pueblo judío.

fr.L: Or il y avait un homme d’entre les Pharisiens, du nom de Nicodème, un chef des Juifs.

vi.L: Bấy giờ có một người thuộc phái Pha-ri-si, tên [người ấy] là Ni-cô-đem, một người lãnh đạo của người Do Thái.
vi.B: Có một người tên là Ni-cô-đem, thuộc phái Pha-ri-si, là một trong những người lãnh đạo của dân Do Thái.

ko.L: 그런데 바리새파 사람들 가운데 한 사람이 있었다. 그의 이름은 니고데모였고, 유대인들의 지도자였다.

pt.L: Ora, havia um homem dentre os fariseus, Nicodemos [era] o nome dele, um chefe dos judeus.
pt.B: Havia um homem chamado Nicodemos, fariseu e um dos líderes do povo judeu.
pt.R: Havia um homem chamado Nicodemos. Ele era fariseu e um dos líderes do povo judeu.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, among whom he was a leader
alternatives: the Jewish authorities as a group opposed to Jesus
decisions.reason: John uses the word in several senses (see the note on the book's terms). Here it names the people Nicodemus was a ruler of, so it means the Jewish people as a whole. Nicodemus himself is a Jew, as are Jesus and his disciples.

decisions.choice: a ruler: one of the leading men of the nation, most likely a member of the council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: In John the "rulers" are the leading men in Jerusalem, named alongside the Pharisees (7:26, 48; 12:42). In 7:50-51 Nicodemus speaks up among the chief priests and Pharisees when they meet in council, so he belonged to the governing body of the Jews in Jerusalem, which met under the high priest.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: the movement devoted to keeping the law exactly
decisions.reason: See the note at 1:24. The Pharisees had already questioned John the Baptist (1:24-25); now one of them comes to Jesus.

decisions.choice: a man: the story continues from 2:24-25
alternatives: a new story with no link to what comes before
decisions.reason: Chapter 2 ended with Jesus knowing "what was in man" (2:25), using the same word. John opens with "a man" and "now", so Nicodemus comes as one example of the people of 2:23-25 whose belief rested on signs (3:2).

decisions.choice: Nicodemus [was] his name
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek way of giving a name ("Nicodemus, name to him") and brackets the verb English needs.

decisions.choice: one of the leaders of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "ruler" means and name the people he led (meaning decisions m1 and m2). Literal keeps the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: uno de los dirigentes del pueblo judío
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what "ruler" means and name the people he led (meaning decisions m1 and m2). Here the word means the people, so it is "el pueblo judío", not "los dirigentes judíos" as in 1:19.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (3:1-36), as in 1:19 and 2:1. The passé simple ("vint", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (3:4 "Nicodème lui dit"), as the English Literal does; with "dire" the present and the passé simple look the same. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus a répondu"). Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je t'ai dit", "Dieu a aimé"), and the imperfect for what was going on ("Jean baptisait").

decisions.choice: un chef des Juifs (L); l'un des chefs du peuple juif (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people, among whom Nicodemus was a leader (meaning decisions m1 and m2), so Balanced and Readable say "le peuple juif" and do not use "les chefs juifs", the book-wide wording for the authorities in Jerusalem. Literal keeps the word John wrote. "Du nom de" (L) is the French way of giving a name in passing, so Literal needs no bracketed verb.

source.text: οὗτος ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐλήλυθας διδάσκαλος· οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται ταῦτα τὰ σημεῖα ποιεῖν ἃ σὺ ποιεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ ὁ θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This one came to him by night and said to him, "Rabbi, we know that from God you have come [as] teacher; no one for is able these the signs to do which you do, if not may be the God with him."

en.L: He came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by night and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have come from God [as a] teacher; for no one is able to do these signs that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do, unless God is with {{gender:them|him}}."
en.B: He came to Jesus at night and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have come from God as a teacher, because no one can do such signs as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do unless God is with {{gender:them|him}}."
en.R: One night he came to see Jesus. He said, "Rabbi, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a teacher God has sent. No one could do the signs {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do unless God was with {{gender:them|him}}."

es.L: Este vino a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de noche y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabí, sabemos que has venido de Dios [como] maestro; porque nadie puede hacer estas señales que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} haces si Dios no está con {{gender:esa persona|él}}».
es.B: Fue a ver a Jesús de noche y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabí, sabemos que eres un maestro que ha venido de Dios, porque nadie puede hacer las señales que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} haces si Dios no está con {{gender:quien las hace|él}}».
es.R: Una noche fue a ver a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabí, sabemos que eres un maestro enviado por Dios. Solo alguien que tiene a Dios de su lado podría hacer las señales que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} haces».

fr.L: Celui-ci vint vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de nuit et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbi, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es venu de Dieu [comme] maître ; car personne ne peut faire ces signes que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais, si Dieu n’est pas avec lui. »
fr.B: Il vint trouver Jésus de nuit et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbi, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un maître venu de Dieu, car personne ne peut accomplir les signes que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} accomplis si Dieu n’est pas avec lui. »
fr.R: Une nuit, il est allé voir Jésus. Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Rabbi, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un maître envoyé par Dieu. Personne ne pourrait faire les signes que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais si Dieu n’était pas avec lui. »

sw.L: Huyo alikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} usiku, akamwambia, "Rabi, tunajua kwamba umekuja kutoka kwa Mungu [ukiwa] mwalimu; kwa maana hakuna mtu awezaye kufanya ishara hizi unazozifanya {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, isipokuwa Mungu awe pamoja naye."
sw.B: Alimjia Yesu usiku, akamwambia, "Rabi, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwalimu uliyetoka kwa Mungu, kwa sababu hakuna mtu anayeweza kufanya ishara kama unazofanya {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} isipokuwa Mungu yu pamoja naye."
sw.R: Usiku mmoja alikwenda kumwona Yesu. Akasema, "Rabi, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwalimu aliyetumwa na Mungu. Hakuna mtu ambaye angeweza kufanya ishara unazofanya, isipokuwa Mungu awe pamoja naye."

vi.L: Người này đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban đêm và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, chúng tôi biết rằng Thầy đã từ Đức Chúa Trời đến [làm] người dạy dỗ; vì không ai có thể làm những dấu lạ này mà Thầy làm, nếu Đức Chúa Trời không ở cùng người ấy."
vi.B: Ông đến gặp Đức Giê-xu ban đêm và thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người dạy dỗ từ Đức Chúa Trời đến, vì không ai làm được những dấu lạ như Thầy làm, nếu Đức Chúa Trời không ở với người ấy."
vi.R: Một đêm kia, ông đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Ông nói: "Thưa Ra-bi, chúng tôi biết Thầy là thầy dạy được Đức Chúa Trời sai đến. Nếu Đức Chúa Trời không ở cùng, chẳng ai làm được những dấu lạ Thầy làm."

ko.L: 이 사람이 밤에 그분께 와서 그분께 말했다. "랍비, 우리는 선생님께서 하나님께로부터 오신 스승이심을 압니다. 하나님께서 그 사람과 함께 계시지 않으면, 아무도 선생님께서 행하시는 이 표적들을 행할 수 없기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 그가 밤에 예수께 와서 말했다. "랍비님, 우리는 선생님께서 하나님께로부터 오신 스승이심을 압니다. 하나님께서 함께하시지 않으면, 아무도 선생님께서 행하시는 이런 표적들을 행할 수 없기 때문입니다."
ko.R: 어느 날 밤, 그가 예수를 찾아와서 말했다. "랍비님, 우리는 선생님이 하나님께서 보내신 스승이라는 것을 압니다. 하나님께서 함께하시지 않는다면, 아무도 선생님처럼 표적들을 행할 수 없습니다."

pt.L: Este veio até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} de noite e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Rabi, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vieste da parte de Deus [como] mestre; pois ninguém pode fazer estes sinais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fazes, se Deus não estiver com ele."
pt.B: Ele veio até Jesus de noite e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Rabi, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vieste da parte de Deus como mestre, porque ninguém pode fazer os sinais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fazes se Deus não estiver com ele."
pt.R: Uma noite, ele foi ver Jesus. Ele disse: "Rabi, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és um mestre enviado por Deus. Ninguém poderia fazer os sinais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fazes se Deus não estivesse com ele."

decisions.choice: by night: a plain note of time that John also gives a deeper sense
alternatives: a sign that Nicodemus came in secret, out of fear
a quiet time chosen for a long talk
decisions.reason: John recalls the detail twice (19:39, "who had first come to him by night"), so it matters to him. Rulers who believed were afraid to say so openly (12:42), which suggests secrecy, but the text does not give a motive. In this Gospel night and darkness stand for life away from the light (1:5; 9:4; 11:10; 13:30, "and it was night"), and the talk ends with people who come to the light or stay away from it (3:19-21). Every level keeps "at night" and draws no conclusion about his reasons.

decisions.choice: we know: Nicodemus speaks for others too
alternatives: a polite plural for himself alone
decisions.reason: The plural suggests he speaks for a group, perhaps fellow Pharisees or the people of 2:23 who believed when they saw his signs. Jesus answers in the plural in 3:7 and 3:11-12.

decisions.choice: signs: the deeds of 2:23 that point to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Key term. Nicodemus draws a right but limited conclusion from the signs: God must be with this teacher (compare 9:16, 33). John has just said that belief based only on signs is not enough (2:23-25); Jesus's answer moves to what Nicodemus does not yet see.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a respectful title for a teacher
decisions.reason: See the note at 1:38. A ruler and a known teacher (3:10) gives this title to a teacher without formal training (compare 7:15), and so honors him.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last person named was Nicodemus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "No one ... unless God is with him" is a general rule about anyone, so the gender setting applies. The pronoun is not about Jesus, so it is not a deity pronoun.

decisions.choice: a teacher God has sent
alternatives: have come from God as a teacher
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "come from God" means here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}} (L); {{gender:quien las hace|él}} (B); no setting (R)
decisions.reason: The rule is about anyone, so the inclusive default avoids a generic "él", which could also be read as Jesus. Readable says it without a pronoun. In this passage Spanish needs the gender setting less often than English: "alguien", "nadie" and the verb forms are already general.

decisions.choice: Jesús
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last person named was Nicodemus.

decisions.choice: si Dieu n'est pas avec lui, with no gender setting on the pronoun
decisions.reason: The rule is about anyone, man or woman, and the English uses the gender setting here. In French a pronoun that picks up "personne" (no one), "quelqu'un", "quiconque" or "celui qui" is masculine whatever the person, and reads as "anyone"; "cette personne" would clash with "personne" in the same sentence, and "lui ou elle" does not suit this register. The possessives "son", "sa", "ses" and the indirect "lui" (to him or her) do not mark gender at all. So in this chapter the gender setting is used where French has a choice of words ("quelqu'un" or "un homme", "les humains" or "les hommes", 3:3, 3:5, 3:19, 3:27), not on these pronouns (3:18, 3:20-21, 3:33, 3:36). A native reviewer should confirm this approach.

decisions.choice: maître
decisions.reason: As in 1:38, where John translates "Rabbi": "maître" is the French word for a teacher one respects. "Enseignant" names a job, and "docteur" (the old word for a teacher of the Law) now means a physician. Verse 10 uses the same word for Nicodemus.

decisions.choice: forms of address in 3:1-21: Nicodemus calls Jesus "Thầy" (after "Thưa Ra-bi") and himself "chúng tôi"; Jesus says "Ta" and calls him "ông"
decisions.reason: Nicodemus comes respectfully to a teacher, so "Thầy" (which is what Rabbi means) fits; he is not a disciple, so he says "chúng tôi", not "chúng con". Jesus speaks to an older, senior man as "ông".

decisions.choice: "người ấy" for "him" (whoever does such signs), with no gender span
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: "Người ấy" (that person) is already inclusive, so Vietnamese has only one way to say it and no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: Narrative honorifics for Jesus ("께", "-시-", "그분"); no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: deity_pronoun setting spans, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and for God is carried at every level by "께서", the honorific "-시-" and "그분". This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: Nicodemus speaks in the formal polite style and says "선생님" for "you"; "랍비" (L), "랍비님" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "당신" to a respected person sounds cold or even quarrelsome in Korean; a title is the polite way to say "you". Nicodemus honours Jesus as a teacher, so he uses the formal style ("-습니다") with honorifics. "스승" is used for the noun "teacher" so it does not clash with the address "선생님".

decisions.choice: no gender setting on generic words: "ninguém ... com ele", "alguém", "quem", "todo aquele que"
decisions.reason: Through this chapter the English needs a gender span for "they/he" after "no one", "someone" and "whoever" (3:2, 3, 5, 18, 20, 21, 27, 33, 36). Portuguese "ninguém", "alguém", "quem" and "todo aquele que" already mean anyone, and the "ele" that refers back to them is ordinary generic Portuguese (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), so no setting is used there. The setting stays where Portuguese must choose a noun, as for the Greek word for a human being in 3:19 and 3:27.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν, οὐ δύναται ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said to him, "Amen, amen I say to you, if not someone be born from above, not he is able to see the kingdom of the God."

en.L: Jesus answered and said to him, "Truly, truly I say to you, unless {{gender:someone|a man}} is born from above, {{gender:they|he}} cannot see the kingdom of God."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless {{gender:someone|a man}} is born from above, {{gender:they|he}} cannot see the kingdom of God."
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: no one can see God's kingdom unless God gives {{gender:them|him}} a new birth from above."

es.L: Respondió Jesús y le dijo: «En verdad, en verdad te digo que, si alguien no nace de lo alto, no puede ver el reino de Dios».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «En verdad, en verdad te digo que, si alguien no nace de lo alto, no puede ver el reino de Dios».
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Te digo la verdad: nadie puede ver el reino de Dios si Dios no le da un nuevo nacimiento de lo alto».

fr.L: Jésus répondit et lui dit : « En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis, si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} ne naît d’en haut, il ne peut voir le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis : si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} ne naît pas d’en haut, il ne peut pas voir le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Je te le dis, c’est la vérité : {{gender:personne|aucun homme}} ne peut voir le royaume de Dieu si Dieu ne lui donne pas une nouvelle naissance d’en haut. »

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, akamwambia, "Kweli kweli nakuambia, mtu asipozaliwa kutoka juu, hawezi kuuona ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Kweli kweli nakuambia, mtu asipozaliwa kutoka juu, hawezi kuuona ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Nakuambia ukweli: hakuna mtu awezaye kuuona ufalme wa Mungu, isipokuwa Mungu amzae upya kutoka juu."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp và nói với ông: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với ông, nếu một người không được sinh ra từ trên cao, thì không thể thấy vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với ông, nếu ai không được sinh ra từ trên cao thì không thể thấy vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ta nói thật với ông: không ai có thể thấy vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời nếu Đức Chúa Trời không cho người ấy được sinh ra một lần nữa từ trên cao."

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 네게 말한다. 누구든지 위로부터 태어나지 않으면, 하나님의 나라를 볼 수 없다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "진실로 진실로 네게 말한다. 누구든지 위로부터 태어나지 않으면 하나님의 나라를 볼 수 없다."

pt.L: Jesus respondeu e lhe disse: "Em verdade, em verdade eu lhe digo: se alguém não nascer do alto, não pode ver o Reino de Deus."

decisions.choice: from above, with "again" also in view: a double meaning that Nicodemus hears only one way
decisions.reason: ἄνωθεν can mean "from above" (3:31; 19:11; 19:23, of a robe woven from the top) or "again, anew" (Galatians 4:9). Everywhere else in John it means from above, and the birth Jesus describes comes from God (1:13) and from the Spirit (3:5-8). Nicodemus hears "a second time" (3:4). Both senses are true of what Jesus means: a new birth that comes from God. The other side: "again" is the familiar rendering and fits Nicodemus's reply, and some early readers took it so.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: God's rule and the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: This phrase is common in Matthew, Mark and Luke but appears in John only here and in 3:5. In the rest of the conversation Jesus speaks instead of eternal life (3:15-16, 36), which is John's usual way of describing the same gift.

decisions.choice: see: experience, have a part in
decisions.reason: To "see" the kingdom is to share in it; 3:5 says "enter", and 3:36 speaks of "seeing life" in the same way.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers the question behind Nicodemus's words
decisions.reason: Nicodemus has not asked anything. Jesus replies to what lies behind his opening, as one who knows what is in a person (2:25): seeing signs is not enough to see God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: τις is general, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 3:5 and 3:11 as well.

decisions.choice: born from above
decisions.reason: No single word carries both senses of the Greek (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced give the sense John uses elsewhere; it departs from the familiar "born again", so the footnote gives that rendering.

decisions.choice: unless God gives them a new birth from above
alternatives: unless they are born from above
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives the birth, which "from above" means (1:13), and says "a new birth from above" so that both senses of the word are kept. The order is turned round so the sentence is simpler.

decisions.choice: {{gender:someone|a man}} ... {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: Inclusive default; the traditional form one tap away.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad te digo (L, B); Te digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering (see 1:51), here with the singular "te" because Jesus speaks to Nicodemus. It covers 3:5 and 3:11.

decisions.choice: nacer de lo alto
decisions.reason: No single Spanish word carries both senses of the Greek (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced give the sense John uses elsewhere; it departs from the familiar "nacer de nuevo", so the footnote gives that reading.

decisions.choice: si Dios no le da un nuevo nacimiento de lo alto
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names God as the one who gives the birth and keeps both senses with "nuevo nacimiento de lo alto".

decisions.choice: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis (L, B); Je te le dis, c'est la vérité (R)
alternatives: Amen, amen, je te le dis
Oui, vraiment, je te le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 3:5 and 3:11 as well. Jesus speaks to Nicodemus alone, so French says "te", not "vous". Readable puts the pledge in plain words.

decisions.choice: naître d'en haut (L, B); une nouvelle naissance d'en haut (R)
decisions.reason: French has no single word for both senses of the Greek (meaning decision m1): "d'en haut" says where the birth comes from, "de nouveau" that it is a second one. Literal and Balanced give the sense John uses elsewhere, as the English does, and depart from the familiar "naître de nouveau", which the footnote gives. Readable adds "nouvelle", so that both senses are heard, and names God as the giver, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:quelqu'un|un homme}} (L, B); {{gender:personne|aucun homme}} (R)
decisions.reason: Anyone, man or woman (meaning decision m5): the inclusive default, with the traditional wording as the alternative. The "il" that follows is the generic French pronoun (see verse 2).

decisions.choice: kutoka juu (L, B); upya kutoka juu (R)
decisions.reason: ἄνωθεν means "from above" and can also mean "again", and the meaning note keeps both. Swahili has no word for both. Literal and Balanced say "kutoka juu" (from above), the sense Jesus means; Nicodemus's "mara ya pili" (a second time) in verse 4 shows how he heard it. Readable says "upya kutoka juu" (anew, from above), which carries both.

decisions.choice: no gender spans in this chapter
decisions.reason: The English needs "someone ... they" with "a man ... he" as the traditional alternative. Swahili "mtu" (a person) and its verbs (a-sipozaliwa, ha-wezi) say nothing about sex, so there is nothing for the setting to change, here or in the rest of the chapter.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với ông" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với ông" (R), for the whole passage
decisions.reason: The book-wide form from the style guide; Readable uses the plain spoken way of stressing that something is true.

decisions.choice: "sinh ra từ trên cao"; Readable adds "một lần nữa"
decisions.reason: No Vietnamese word means both "from above" and "again". "Từ trên cao" gives the sense Jesus means; Nicodemus's "lần thứ hai" in verse 4 shows the other hearing, and the footnote explains. Readable keeps both senses by saying both.

decisions.choice: "một người", "ai", "người ấy" with no gender spans (whole passage)
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese words for people are already inclusive (style guide section 7), so the English gender spans of 3:3-36 have no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "진실로 진실로 네게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide form for "Truly, truly" in Korean, used through this passage (3:3, 3:5, 3:11). Here the Greek "you" is singular, Nicodemus alone, so the guide's "너희에게" becomes "네게".

decisions.choice: "위로부터 태어나다"; "위로부터 새로 태어나다" (R)
decisions.reason: No Korean word means both "from above" and "again" as the Greek does. "위로부터" keeps Jesus's primary sense (birth from God); the familiar "거듭나다" says only "again", the sense Nicodemus hears in 3:4. Readable adds "새로" so the second sense is not lost; the footnote explains the play.

decisions.choice: "누구든지", "아무도", "사람" with no gender spans
alternatives: gender setting spans as in the English
decisions.reason: These Korean words already include men and women, and Korean needs no pronoun where English says "he", so the English gender spans have nothing to change. This holds through the passage (3:2-36).

decisions.choice: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhe digo (L, B); Eu garanto a você (R)
alternatives: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo
decisions.reason: The book-wide formula of 1:51, here in the singular, since Jesus speaks to Nicodemus alone; it covers 3:5 and 3:11 as well. The plural "vocês" in 3:7 and 3:11-12 then shows that the saying reaches beyond him.

decisions.choice: water and Spirit: one birth with two sides, cleansing and new life from God
alternatives: water stands for baptism, and the Spirit for the gift that comes with it
water stands for natural birth, and the Spirit for the second birth
decisions.reason: One preposition governs both nouns, so they describe a single birth. The prophets promised that God would wash his people with clean water and put his Spirit within them (Ezekiel 36:25-27), and a teacher of Israel should know this (3:10). Baptism is also close at hand: John has baptized with water and promised one who baptizes with the Spirit (1:26, 33), and baptism follows in 3:22-26. Some take the water as natural birth (compare 3:6), but a single phrase for two different births is unlikely. Every level keeps "water and the Spirit" without explaining it.

decisions.choice: Spirit: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: There is no article, but the Spirit here is the one who gives the birth (3:6, 8), the Spirit who came down on Jesus (1:32-33).

decisions.choice: the same saying as 3:3, explained

decisions.choice: d'eau et d'Esprit (L); de l'eau et de l'Esprit (B, R)
decisions.reason: French can say "naître d'eau et d'Esprit" without articles, so Literal shows that the Greek has none, and that one preposition joins the two nouns into a single birth (meaning decision m1), without brackets. Balanced and Readable use the articles of ordinary French, as the English does.

vi.R: Cha mẹ loài người sinh ra con cái có sự sống của loài người. Còn những ai được Thánh Linh sinh ra thì có sự sống của Thánh Linh.

ko.L: 육으로부터 태어난 것은 육이고, 성령으로부터 태어난 것은 영이다.
ko.B: 육으로 태어난 것은 무엇이든 육이고, 성령으로 태어난 것은 무엇이든 영이다.
ko.R: 사람은 부모에게서 사람의 생명을 받아 태어난다. 그러나 성령으로 태어난 사람은 성령께서 주시는 생명을 얻는다.

pt.L: O que nasceu da carne é carne, e o que nasceu do Espírito é espírito.
pt.B: O que nasce da carne é carne, e o que nasce do Espírito é espírito.
pt.R: Pais humanos dão aos filhos uma vida humana. Mas quem nasce do Espírito tem a vida do Espírito.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature, weak and mortal, as it comes by natural birth
decisions.reason: In John σάρξ means ordinary human existence (1:13-14, "the Word became flesh"; 6:63; 17:2), not sin as often in Paul. Natural birth gives natural life; it cannot produce the life of God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: the Spirit (the Holy Spirit) gives spirit (a life that belongs to God)
decisions.reason: The first is the Holy Spirit, who gives the birth (3:5). The second names what is born: a life of the Spirit's own kind (compare 4:24; 6:63). Like produces like.

decisions.choice: a general rule: whatever is born
decisions.reason: The neuter "what is born" states a principle that covers every person.

decisions.choice: Whatever is born
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the general rule in plain words.

decisions.choice: Human parents give their children a human life ... the Spirit's life
alternatives: What is born of the flesh is flesh
decisions.reason: "Flesh is flesh" means little to young readers; Readable says what natural birth gives and what the Spirit gives (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: Los padres humanos dan a sus hijos una vida humana ... la vida del Espíritu
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what natural birth gives and what the Spirit gives (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: "linh" (lowercase) for the spirit born of the Spirit
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps lowercase "linh" where the word is not the Holy Spirit. "Thần" now suggests a god or ghost, and "tâm linh" the inner life, which is narrower than the life from God meant here.

decisions.choice: "육" for flesh; "성령" (the Holy Spirit) and "영" (spirit)
decisions.reason: "육" is human nature as it comes by natural birth, not only the body that "몸" or "육체" would name. The Korean distinction between "성령" and "영" shows the two senses of the one Greek word that the meaning decision explains.

source.text: μὴ θαυμάσῃς ὅτι εἶπόν σοι Δεῖ ὑμᾶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν.

records.literal_gloss: Not do marvel that I said to you, 'It is necessary for you [all] to be born from above.'

en.L: Do not marvel that I said to you, 'It is necessary for you [all] to be born from above.'
en.B: Do not be surprised that I told you, 'All of you must be born from above.'
en.R: Do not be surprised that I said, 'All of you need a new birth from above.'

es.L: No te maravilles de que te dije: “Es necesario que {{plural_you:ustedes nazcan|vosotros nazcáis}} de lo alto”.
es.B: No te sorprendas de que te haya dicho: “{{plural_you:Ustedes tienen|Vosotros tenéis}} que nacer de lo alto”.
es.R: No te sorprendas de que te haya dicho: “{{plural_you:Ustedes necesitan|Vosotros necesitáis}} un nuevo nacimiento de lo alto”.

fr.L: Ne t’étonne pas que je t’aie dit : “Il vous faut naître d’en haut.”
fr.B: Ne sois pas surpris que je t’aie dit : “Vous devez tous naître d’en haut.”
fr.R: Ne sois pas étonné que je t’aie dit : “Vous avez tous besoin d’une nouvelle naissance d’en haut.”

sw.L: Usishangae kwa sababu nilikuambia, 'Imewapasa ninyi kuzaliwa kutoka juu.'
sw.B: Usishangae kwamba nilikuambia, 'Ninyi nyote mnapaswa kuzaliwa kutoka juu.'
sw.R: Usishangae kwamba nilisema, 'Ninyi nyote mnahitaji kuzaliwa upya kutoka juu.'

vi.L: Đừng ngạc nhiên vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với ông: 'Các ông cần phải được sinh ra từ trên cao.'
vi.B: Đừng ngạc nhiên khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo ông: 'Tất cả các ông đều phải được sinh ra từ trên cao.'
vi.R: Đừng ngạc nhiên khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói: 'Tất cả các ông đều cần được sinh ra một lần nữa từ trên cao.'

ko.L: 내가 네게 '너희는 위로부터 태어나야 한다'고 말한 것을 이상히 여기지 마라.
ko.B: 내가 네게 '너희는 모두 위로부터 태어나야 한다'고 말했다고 해서 놀라지 마라.
ko.R: 내가 '너희는 모두 위로부터 새로 태어나야 한다'고 말했다고 놀라지 마라.

pt.L: Não se admire de eu lhe ter dito: 'É necessário que vocês nasçam do alto.'
pt.B: Não fique surpreso por eu ter dito a você: 'Todos vocês precisam nascer do alto.'
pt.R: Não fique surpreso por eu ter dito: 'Todos vocês precisam de um novo nascimento, que vem do alto.'

decisions.choice: "to you" is singular, then "you" is plural: the need is for everyone
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Nicodemus (singular), but the saying is for all, including those Nicodemus spoke for with his "we know" (3:2).

decisions.choice: from above, as in 3:3
decisions.reason: See meaning decision m1 at 3:3.

decisions.choice: must: a necessity, not advice
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the Son of Man in 3:14 and of John in 3:30: it is what God's purpose requires.

decisions.choice: [all] (L); All of you (B, R)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: be surprised
decisions.reason: Everyday words; Literal keeps "marvel".

decisions.choice: te ... ustedes / vosotros, no supplied [all]
decisions.reason: Spanish shows both numbers: "te" to Nicodemus, then a plural "you" for everyone (meaning decision m1), so no level needs an added word. The plural takes the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: no te sorprendas (B, R); no te maravilles (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: everyday words; Literal keeps the older verb.

decisions.choice: te ... vous (L); vous ... tous (B, R)
alternatives: [vous tous] at Literal, as the English
decisions.reason: French shows what English cannot: Jesus says "te" to Nicodemus and "vous" for everyone (meaning decision m1), so Literal needs no bracketed word. Balanced and Readable add "tous" to make the point unmistakable, as the English does with "All of you". "Il vous faut" (L) keeps the impersonal "it is necessary" of the Greek, the "il faut" of 3:14 and 3:30.

decisions.choice: usishangae, nilikuambia (singular); imewapasa ninyi (plural)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Nicodemus in the singular, then says the need is for "you" in the plural. Swahili marks the shift in the verbs and pronoun (u-, -ku-, then -wa-, ninyi), so Literal needs no bracketed "[all]"; Balanced and Readable add "nyote" (all), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các ông" with no brackets
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks the plural in the pronoun itself ("ông" to "các ông"), so Literal needs no bracketed word to show that the "you" has become plural.

decisions.choice: "네게" ... "너희는" with no brackets
decisions.reason: Korean marks the change from singular to plural "you" in the pronouns themselves, so Literal needs no supplied "[all]" as the English does.

decisions.choice: vocês, with nothing supplied
decisions.reason: Portuguese "lhe" (to you, one person) and "vocês" (you, several) already show the change from singular to plural that meaning decision m1 describes, so Literal needs no "[all]".

source.text: τὸ πνεῦμα ὅπου θέλει πνεῖ, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἀκούεις, ἀλλ’ οὐκ οἶδας πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει· οὕτως ἐστὶν πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος.

records.literal_gloss: The wind where it wills blows, and the sound of it you hear, but not you know from where it comes and where it goes; thus is everyone the [one] having been born of the Spirit.

en.L: The wind blows where it wills, and its sound you hear, but you do not know from where it comes and where it goes; so is everyone who has been born of the Spirit."
en.B: The wind blows where it wants to. You hear its sound, yet you do not know where it has come from or where it is heading. That is how it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit."
en.R: The wind blows wherever it wants. You can hear it, but you cannot tell where it started or where it will go. It is like that with everyone who is born of the Spirit."

es.L: El viento sopla donde quiere, y oyes su sonido, pero no sabes de dónde viene ni adónde va; así es todo el que ha nacido del Espíritu».
es.B: El viento sopla donde quiere. Oyes su sonido, pero no sabes de dónde viene ni adónde va. Así sucede con todo el que nace del Espíritu».
es.R: El viento sopla por donde quiere. Lo puedes oír, pero no sabes dónde empezó ni adónde irá. Así pasa con todos los que nacen del Espíritu».

fr.L: Le vent souffle là où il veut, et tu entends son bruit, mais tu ne sais pas d’où il vient ni où il va ; ainsi en est-il de quiconque est né de l’Esprit. »
fr.B: Le vent souffle là où il veut. Tu en entends le bruit, mais tu ne sais pas d’où il vient ni où il s’en va. Il en va de même pour quiconque est né de l’Esprit. »
fr.R: Le vent va où il veut. Tu peux l’entendre, mais tu ne peux pas dire d’où il est parti ni où il ira. C’est pareil pour tous ceux qui naissent de l’Esprit. »

sw.L: Upepo unavuma mahali unapotaka, na sauti yake unaisikia, lakini hujui unatoka wapi na unakwenda wapi; hivyo ndivyo ilivyo kwa kila aliyezaliwa kutoka kwa Roho."
sw.B: Upepo huvuma popote unapotaka. Unasikia sauti yake, lakini hujui unakotoka wala unakoelekea. Ndivyo ilivyo kwa kila mtu aliyezaliwa kwa Roho."
sw.R: Upepo huvuma popote unapotaka. Unaweza kuusikia, lakini huwezi kujua ulikoanzia wala utakakokwenda. Ndivyo ilivyo kwa kila mtu aliyezaliwa kwa Roho."

vi.L: Gió thổi nơi nó muốn, và ông nghe tiếng của nó, nhưng không biết nó từ đâu đến và đi đâu; mọi người đã được sinh ra từ Thánh Linh cũng vậy."
vi.B: Gió thổi về nơi nào nó muốn. Ông nghe tiếng gió nhưng không biết gió từ đâu đến và sẽ đi về đâu. Ai được sinh ra bởi Thánh Linh cũng đều như vậy."
vi.R: Gió thổi đến bất cứ nơi đâu nó muốn. Ông nghe được tiếng gió, nhưng không biết gió bắt đầu từ đâu hay sẽ đi đâu. Người được Thánh Linh sinh ra cũng giống như thế."

ko.L: 바람은 원하는 곳으로 불고, 너는 그 소리를 듣지만, 그것이 어디로부터 오며 어디로 가는지 너는 알지 못한다. 성령으로부터 태어난 사람은 누구나 이와 같다."
ko.B: 바람은 불고 싶은 대로 분다. 너는 그 소리를 듣지만, 그 바람이 어디서 불어와 어디로 가는지는 모른다. 성령으로 태어난 사람도 모두 이와 같다."
ko.R: 바람은 자기가 불고 싶은 곳으로 분다. 너는 바람 소리를 들을 수 있지만, 바람이 어디서 시작해서 어디로 가는지는 알 수 없다. 성령으로 태어난 사람도 모두 이와 같다."

pt.L: O vento sopra onde quer, e você ouve o som dele, mas não sabe de onde vem nem para onde vai; assim é todo aquele que nasceu do Espírito."
pt.B: O vento sopra onde quer. Você ouve o seu som, mas não sabe de onde ele vem nem para onde vai. Assim acontece com todo aquele que nasce do Espírito."
pt.R: O vento sopra para onde quer. Você pode ouvi-lo, mas não consegue dizer de onde ele veio nem para onde vai. É assim com todo aquele que nasce do Espírito."

decisions.choice: wind and Spirit: one word, with a play on its two senses
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα means both wind (or breath) and spirit; the verb "blows" comes from the same root. Jesus speaks of the wind and means the Spirit as well, as Ezekiel's vision plays on wind, breath and Spirit giving life to dry bones (Ezekiel 37:9-14). The footnote shows that the two words are one.

decisions.choice: sound, which can also mean voice
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary one for sound or voice: the wind's sound is heard, as the Spirit's work is known by its effects.

decisions.choice: the birth from the Spirit is real, free and beyond human control
alternatives: the person born of the Spirit becomes unpredictable
decisions.reason: As no one controls or tracks the wind but its effects are plain, so it is with the Spirit's work in those he gives birth to. The point is not that such people behave strangely, but that their birth comes from God, not from human doing (1:13).

decisions.choice: wind ... Spirit
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: one word cannot carry both senses here, so the first is "wind" and the last is "Spirit", with the footnote (meaning decision m1). "It" refers to the wind; the Spirit is never called "it".

decisions.choice: where it wills
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb of wanting; Balanced and Readable use "wants".

decisions.choice: viento ... Espíritu
decisions.reason: As in English: Spanish "espíritu" does not mean wind, so the first is "viento" and the last "Espíritu", with the footnote on meaning decision m1 giving the play on words.

decisions.choice: le vent ... l'Esprit
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: one French word cannot carry both senses here (meaning decision m1, whose footnote shows that the Greek has one word). French "souffle" comes close, since it means breath and wind and comes from the verb "souffler", but "le souffle souffle" is clumsy and "le Souffle" for the Holy Spirit is not common usage. "Il" refers to the wind.

decisions.choice: bruit (L, B); l'entendre (R)
decisions.reason: French "voix" is used of people, and of the wind only in poetry; "bruit" is the ordinary word for the sound the wind makes. The other sense of the Greek word is in meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: upepo ... Roho
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα means both wind and spirit, and Jesus plays on it. Swahili "roho" means spirit or soul but never wind, so the verse says "upepo" (wind) and "Roho" (the Spirit), as the English does, and the meaning note explains the play.

decisions.choice: "gió" ... "Thánh Linh"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no word that means both wind and Spirit, so the play on one Greek word cannot be kept; the footnote on the meaning decision explains it.

en.B: Nicodemus asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How can this be possible?"
en.R: Nicodemus asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How can this happen?"

es.L: Respondió Nicodemo y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¿Cómo pueden suceder estas cosas?».
es.B: Nicodemo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Cómo es posible esto?».
es.R: «¿Cómo puede pasar eso?», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó Nicodemo.

fr.B: Nicodème {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demanda : « Comment cela est-il possible ? »
fr.R: Nicodème {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a demandé : « Comment est-ce que cela peut arriver ? »

vi.B: Ni-cô-đem thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Làm sao điều đó có thể được?"

ko.L: 니고데모가 대답하여 그분께 말했다. "이런 일들이 어떻게 일어날 수 있습니까?"
ko.B: 니고데모가 예수께 물었다. "어떻게 그런 일이 있을 수 있습니까?"
ko.R: 니고데모가 예수께 물었다. "어떻게 그런 일이 일어날 수 있습니까?"

pt.L: Nicodemos respondeu e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Como podem acontecer estas coisas?"
pt.B: Nicodemos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntou: "Como isso é possível?"
pt.R: Nicodemos perguntou a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Como isso pode acontecer?"

decisions.choice: these things: the birth from the Spirit Jesus has described
decisions.reason: Nicodemus no longer argues; he asks how. These are his last words in the chapter. He returns in 7:50-51, when he defends Jesus before the council, and in 19:39, when he brings spices for Jesus's burial.

decisions.choice: this
decisions.reason: English refers to one matter with a singular word.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ διδάσκαλος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ταῦτα οὐ γινώσκεις;

en.L: Jesus answered and said to him, "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know these things?
en.B: Jesus answered, "You are the teacher of Israel, and yet you do not understand this?
en.R: Jesus answered, "You are an important teacher of Israel, and you still do not understand this?

es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Tú eres el maestro de Israel, ¿y no entiendes esto?
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Tú eres un maestro importante de Israel, ¿y todavía no entiendes esto?

fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Tu es le maître d’Israël, et tu ne comprends pas cela ?
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Tu es un maître important en Israël, et tu ne comprends toujours pas cela ?

sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Wewe ni mwalimu mashuhuri wa Israeli, na bado huelewi jambo hili?

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp và nói với ông: "Ông là vị thầy của Y-sơ-ra-ên mà ông không biết những điều này sao?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ông là bậc thầy của Y-sơ-ra-ên mà lại không hiểu điều này sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ông là một thầy dạy quan trọng của Y-sơ-ra-ên, vậy mà ông vẫn chưa hiểu điều này sao?

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 이스라엘의 그 선생이면서 이것들을 모르느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너는 이스라엘의 선생이라면서 이것도 깨닫지 못하느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너는 이스라엘의 이름난 선생인데도 아직 이것을 깨닫지 못하느냐?

pt.L: Jesus respondeu e lhe disse: "Você é o mestre de Israel e não conhece estas coisas?
pt.B: Jesus respondeu: "Você é o mestre de Israel e mesmo assim não entende isso?
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Você é um mestre importante de Israel e ainda não entende isso?

decisions.choice: the teacher of Israel: a well-known teacher, perhaps said with some irony
alternatives: a teacher of Israel, one among many
the one chief teacher of the nation
decisions.reason: The article marks Nicodemus as a recognized teacher. He had greeted Jesus as "a teacher come from God" (3:2); now Jesus turns the title back on him.

decisions.choice: a teacher of Israel should have known it from the Scriptures
decisions.reason: The prophets had spoken of God giving a new heart and his Spirit within his people (Ezekiel 36:25-27; Jeremiah 31:33). Jesus is not teaching something unheard of in Israel.

decisions.choice: know: understand
decisions.reason: The verb means to know with understanding; Nicodemus has heard the words but not grasped them.

decisions.choice: an important teacher
decisions.reason: Readable says what the article implies (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: un maestro importante
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what the article implies (meaning decision m1). "Tú" is Nicodemus and has no setting.

decisions.choice: "vị thầy" (L), "bậc thầy" (B), "thầy dạy" (R) for teacher; "Y-sơ-ra-ên" for Israel
decisions.reason: "Giáo sư" now means a professor. "Bậc thầy" carries the article's sense of the well-known teacher. "Y-sơ-ra-ên" is the Protestant form of the name; "Ít-ra-en" is the Catholic one.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to Nicodemus in the plain style ("너", "-느냐")
decisions.reason: The style guide gives Jesus the plain style toward everyone he teaches. Nicodemus is an older leader, and a reviewer may feel the plain style is too blunt for Korean readers; it also matches the gentle rebuke in this verse.

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν, καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἡμῶν οὐ λαμβάνετε.

records.literal_gloss: Amen, amen I say to you that what we know we speak and what we have seen we testify, and the testimony of us not you [all] receive.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, what we know we speak, and what we have seen we testify [to], and our testimony you [all] do not receive.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know and testify to what we have seen, and still you people do not accept our testimony.
en.R: I tell you the truth: we talk about what we know, and we tell about what we have seen. But you people do not accept what we say.

es.L: En verdad, en verdad te digo que lo que sabemos hablamos, y lo que hemos visto testificamos, y {{plural_you:no reciben|no recibís}} nuestro testimonio.
es.B: En verdad, en verdad te digo que hablamos de lo que sabemos y damos testimonio de lo que hemos visto, y aun así {{plural_you:ustedes no aceptan|vosotros no aceptáis}} nuestro testimonio.
es.R: Te digo la verdad: hablamos de lo que sabemos y contamos lo que hemos visto. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no aceptan|vosotros no aceptáis}} lo que decimos.

fr.L: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis : ce que nous savons, nous le disons, et ce que nous avons vu, nous en rendons témoignage ; et notre témoignage, vous ne le recevez pas.
fr.B: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis : nous parlons de ce que nous savons et nous rendons témoignage de ce que nous avons vu, et pourtant vous ne recevez pas notre témoignage.
fr.R: Je te le dis, c’est la vérité : nous parlons de ce que nous savons, et nous racontons ce que nous avons vu. Mais vous n’acceptez pas ce que nous disons.

sw.L: Kweli kweli nakuambia, tunachokijua tunakinena, na tulichokiona tunakishuhudia, na ushuhuda wetu hamuupokei.
sw.B: Kweli kweli nakuambia, tunasema yale tunayoyajua na kushuhudia yale tuliyoyaona, lakini ninyi bado hamuukubali ushuhuda wetu.
sw.R: Nakuambia ukweli: tunazungumza juu ya yale tunayoyajua, na tunasema yale tuliyoyaona. Lakini ninyi hamyakubali tunayoyasema.

vi.L: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với ông, điều chúng tôi biết thì chúng tôi nói, và điều chúng tôi đã thấy thì chúng tôi làm chứng, và lời chứng của chúng tôi thì các ông không nhận.
vi.B: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với ông, chúng tôi nói điều chúng tôi biết và làm chứng điều chúng tôi đã thấy, vậy mà các ông vẫn không nhận lời chứng của chúng tôi.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với ông: chúng tôi nói về điều chúng tôi biết, và kể lại điều chúng tôi đã thấy. Nhưng các ông không chịu nhận lời chúng tôi nói.

ko.L: 진실로 진실로 네게 말한다. 우리가 아는 것을 우리는 말하고, 우리가 본 것을 증언한다. 그런데 우리의 증언을 너희는 받아들이지 않는다.
ko.B: 진실로 진실로 네게 말한다. 우리는 우리가 아는 것을 말하고, 우리가 본 것을 증언한다. 그런데도 너희는 우리의 증언을 받아들이지 않는다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 우리는 우리가 아는 것을 말하고, 우리가 본 것을 전한다. 그런데 너희는 우리 말을 받아들이지 않는다.

pt.L: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhe digo que o que sabemos falamos, e o que vimos testemunhamos, e o nosso testemunho vocês não recebem.
pt.B: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhe digo: nós falamos do que sabemos e damos testemunho do que vimos, e mesmo assim vocês não aceitam o nosso testemunho.
pt.R: Eu garanto a você: nós falamos do que sabemos e contamos o que vimos. Mas vocês não aceitam o que dizemos.

decisions.choice: we: Jesus speaks in the plural, and who is included is not clear
alternatives: Jesus and John the Baptist, both witnesses
a reply in kind to Nicodemus's "we know"
decisions.reason: Jesus switches from "I" to "we" and back to "I" (3:12). He may be answering Nicodemus's "we know" (3:2) with a "we" of his own, or joining others who testify, as the Father and John do (5:31-37). The text does not say, so every level keeps "we".

decisions.choice: you: plural, Nicodemus and those he speaks for
decisions.reason: "I say to you" is singular, but "you do not receive" is plural, as in 3:7.

decisions.choice: testify, testimony: witness given as evidence, as in a court
decisions.reason: The words of 1:7 and 1:19. Jesus speaks of what he knows firsthand, as a witness does; to "receive" his testimony is to accept it as true (3:32-33; compare 1:11-12).

decisions.choice: you people
decisions.reason: Shows the plural (meaning decision m2); Literal uses [all].

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros, no supplied word
decisions.reason: The verb shows the plural (meaning decision m2), so Spanish needs no "[all]" or "you people".

decisions.choice: vous, with no added word
decisions.reason: As in verse 7: French "vous", set against "je te le dis", shows the plural (meaning decision m2), so no level needs the English "[all]" or "you people". Literal and Balanced keep "recevoir", the verb of 1:11-12 ("les siens ne l'ont pas reçu"); Readable says "accepter".

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" (we, not including the hearer)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether "we" includes the person spoken to. Nicodemus and "you people" are set against this "we", so it cannot be "chúng ta"; who else is included is left open, as the meaning decision says.

source.text: εἰ τὰ ἐπίγεια εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια πιστεύσετε;

records.literal_gloss: If the earthly things I told you [all] and not you believe, how if I tell you the heavenly things will you believe?

en.L: If earthly things I told you [all] and you do not believe, how, if I tell you heavenly things, will you believe?
en.B: If you do not believe when I tell you about things on earth, how will you believe when I tell you about things in heaven?
en.R: I have told you about things that happen here on earth, and you do not believe. So how will you believe if I tell you about the things of heaven?

es.L: Si {{plural_you:les|os}} dije las cosas terrenales y no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}, ¿cómo {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}} si {{plural_you:les|os}} digo las celestiales?
es.B: Si no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} hablo de las cosas de la tierra, ¿cómo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}} cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} hable de las cosas del cielo?
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he hablado de cosas que pasan aquí en la tierra, y no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:van|vais}} a creer si {{plural_you:les|os}} hablo de las cosas del cielo?

fr.L: Si je vous ai dit les choses terrestres et que vous ne croyez pas, comment, si je vous dis les choses célestes, croirez-vous ?
fr.B: Si vous ne croyez pas quand je vous parle des choses de la terre, comment croirez-vous quand je vous parlerai des choses du ciel ?
fr.R: Je vous ai parlé de choses qui arrivent ici sur la terre, et vous ne croyez pas. Alors comment croirez-vous si je vous parle des choses du ciel ?

sw.L: Ikiwa mambo ya kidunia niliwaambia, nanyi hamuamini, mtaaminije nikiwaambia mambo ya kimbingu?
sw.B: Ikiwa hamuamini ninapowaeleza mambo yanayotokea duniani, mtaaminije nitakapowaeleza mambo ya mbinguni?
sw.R: Nimewaambia mambo yanayotokea hapa duniani, nanyi hamuamini. Basi mtaaminije nikiwaambia mambo ya mbinguni?

vi.L: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các ông những việc dưới đất mà các ông không tin, thì làm sao các ông sẽ tin nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các ông những việc trên trời?
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các ông về những việc dưới đất mà các ông không tin, thì làm sao các ông tin được khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói về những việc trên trời?
vi.R: Ta đã nói với các ông về những việc xảy ra ngay dưới đất này, mà các ông không tin. Vậy nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói về những việc trên trời, làm sao các ông tin được?

ko.L: 땅의 것들을 내가 너희에게 말했는데 너희가 믿지 않는다면, 하늘의 것들을 내가 너희에게 말할 때 너희가 어떻게 믿겠느냐?
ko.B: 너희는 내가 땅에서 일어나는 일을 말해도 믿지 않는다. 그러니 하늘에 속한 일을 말하면 어떻게 믿겠느냐?
ko.R: 나는 이 땅에서 일어나는 일들을 너희에게 말해 주었다. 그런데도 너희는 믿지 않는다. 그러니 하늘에 있는 일들을 말해 주면 어떻게 믿겠느냐?

pt.L: Se eu lhes falei das coisas terrenas e vocês não creem, como crerão se eu lhes falar das celestiais?
pt.B: Se vocês não creem quando eu lhes falo de coisas da terra, como vão crer quando eu lhes falar de coisas do céu?
pt.R: Eu falei a vocês sobre coisas que acontecem aqui na terra, e vocês não acreditam. Então como vão acreditar se eu falar a vocês sobre as coisas do céu?

decisions.choice: earthly things: what happens on earth, such as the new birth; heavenly things: what belongs to God's own realm
alternatives: earthly things are things told in earthly pictures (birth, wind)
earthly things are ordinary, unimportant matters
decisions.reason: The new birth happens to people here on earth, and Jesus has explained it with earthly pictures. The heavenly things are what follows: the Son of Man who came down from heaven, his lifting up, and God's love in giving him (3:13-16).

decisions.choice: the first "if" states a fact: you do not believe
decisions.reason: The first condition describes what is actually happening; the second looks ahead to what Jesus is about to say.

decisions.choice: believe: accept what he says as true
decisions.reason: Key term. Here the verb has no "in": the question is whether they believe his words (compare 2:22).

decisions.choice: me creen
decisions.reason: The verb here has no "in": the question is whether they believe what he says (meaning decision m3), so Spanish says "creer" + the person, not "creer en".

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: And no one has gone up into the heaven except the [one] out of the heaven having come down, the Son of the Man.

en.L: And no one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down out of heaven, the Son of Man.
en.B: No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man.
en.R: No one has ever gone up into heaven except the Son of Man. He is the one who came down from heaven.

es.L: Y nadie ha subido al cielo, sino el que bajó del cielo, el Hijo del Hombre.
es.B: Nadie ha subido al cielo, sino el que bajó del cielo, el Hijo del Hombre.
es.R: Nadie ha subido jamás al cielo, excepto el Hijo del Hombre. Él es el que bajó del cielo.

fr.L: Et personne n’est monté au ciel, sinon celui qui est descendu du ciel, le Fils de l’homme.
fr.B: Personne n’est monté au ciel, sauf celui qui est descendu du ciel, le Fils de l’homme.
fr.R: Personne n’est jamais monté au ciel, sauf le Fils de l’homme. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui est descendu du ciel.

sw.L: Na hakuna aliyepanda kwenda mbinguni isipokuwa yule aliyeshuka kutoka mbinguni, Mwana wa Adamu.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kupanda mbinguni isipokuwa yule aliyeshuka kutoka mbinguni, yaani Mwana wa Adamu.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kupanda kwenda mbinguni isipokuwa Mwana wa Adamu. Yeye ndiye aliyeshuka kutoka mbinguni.

vi.L: Và chưa ai đã lên trời, ngoại trừ Đấng đã từ trời xuống, Con Người.
vi.B: Chưa ai từng lên trời, ngoại trừ Đấng từ trời xuống, tức là Con Người.
vi.R: Chưa từng có ai lên trời, ngoại trừ Con Người. Ngài là Đấng đã từ trời xuống.

ko.L: 그리고 하늘에서 내려온 이, 곧 인자 말고는 아무도 하늘로 올라간 적이 없다.
ko.B: 하늘에서 내려온 인자 말고는 아무도 하늘에 올라간 적이 없다.
ko.R: 인자, 곧 사람의 아들 말고는 아무도 하늘에 올라가 본 적이 없다. 인자는 하늘에서 내려온 사람이다.

pt.L: E ninguém subiu ao céu, a não ser aquele que desceu do céu, o Filho do Homem.
pt.B: Ninguém subiu ao céu, a não ser aquele que desceu do céu, o Filho do Homem.
pt.R: Ninguém jamais subiu ao céu, a não ser o Filho do Homem. Ele é aquele que desceu do céu.

decisions.choice: only the one who came down from heaven can speak of heavenly things
alternatives: spoken from after Jesus's ascension: no one has gone up except the Son of Man, who first came down
decisions.reason: The sentence answers 3:12: no one has gone up to heaven and come back to tell of it; only the one who came down from there knows heavenly things (compare 1:18). The perfect "has gone up" can also be read as looking back from after Jesus's return to the Father (6:62; 20:17), which would suit the view that from here on the evangelist is speaking (see 3:16). Every level keeps the plain wording.

decisions.choice: Proverbs 30:4 and Deuteronomy 30:12
decisions.reason: "Who has gone up to heaven and come down?" (Proverbs 30:4) asks who can know God's ways; Deuteronomy 30:12 says the law is not in heaven, that someone must go up to fetch it. Jesus's answer is that the one who knows heaven has come down from it.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's title for himself, here as the one from heaven
decisions.reason: See the note at 1:51. In John the Son of Man has come down from heaven (6:62) and will be lifted up (3:14; 8:28; 12:34).

decisions.choice: ends with "the Son of Man" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: adds "who is in heaven" (many later manuscripts)
adds "who was in heaven" (a few early translations)
decisions.reason: The papyri P66 and P75 and Codices Sinaiticus and Vaticanus end the verse with "the Son of Man". Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "who is in heaven"; a few versions read "who was in heaven". Some have defended the longer reading as the harder one. The footnote gives it. A reviewer should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: gone up ... came down
decisions.reason: The same plain verbs as in 1:51 ("going up and coming down"), so the link between the two sayings stays visible.

decisions.choice: subir ... bajar
decisions.reason: The same plain verbs as in 1:51 ("subiendo y bajando"), so the link between the two sayings stays visible.

decisions.choice: C'est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui est descendu
decisions.reason: Readable makes the clause a sentence of its own, as the English does; French marks "he is the one" with "c'est lui", a pronoun for Christ, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "인자, 곧 사람의 아들" (R, once in this passage)
decisions.reason: "인자" is the settled Korean title at every level, but new readers may not know that it means "son of man". Readable spells it out once in the passage, as the style guide allows; it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: No honorific "-시-" when Jesus speaks of himself ("내려온", not "내려오신")
decisions.reason: Korean speakers do not honour themselves. Jesus speaks of the Son of Man, himself, in plain forms, while the narrator and others honour him.

source.text: καὶ καθὼς Μωϋσῆς ὕψωσεν τὸν ὄφιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οὕτως ὑψωθῆναι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, thus to be lifted up it is necessary the Son of the Man, \v 15 so that everyone the [one] believing in him may have life eternal.

en.L: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so it is necessary for the Son of Man to be lifted up, \v 15 so that everyone who believes may in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} have eternal life.
en.B: Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, and in the same way the Son of Man must be lifted up, \v 15 so that everyone who believes will have eternal life in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Long ago in the desert, Moses lifted up a bronze snake on a pole. In the same way, the Son of Man must be lifted up, \v 15 so that everyone who believes can have eternal life in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: the life of the age to come, which begins now.

es.L: Y como Moisés levantó en alto la serpiente en el desierto, así es necesario que el Hijo del Hombre sea levantado en alto, \v 15 para que todo el que cree tenga en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vida eterna.
es.B: Moisés levantó en alto la serpiente en el desierto, y del mismo modo el Hijo del Hombre tiene que ser levantado en alto, \v 15 para que todo el que cree tenga vida eterna en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo, en el desierto, Moisés levantó en alto una serpiente de bronce sobre un poste. Del mismo modo, el Hijo del Hombre tiene que ser levantado en alto, \v 15 para que todo el que cree tenga vida eterna en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya.

fr.L: Et comme Moïse a élevé le serpent dans le désert, ainsi il faut que le Fils de l’homme soit élevé, \v 15 afin que quiconque croit ait en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Moïse a élevé le serpent dans le désert ; de la même manière, il faut que le Fils de l’homme soit élevé, \v 15 pour que quiconque croit ait la vie éternelle en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Il y a très longtemps, dans le désert, Moïse a élevé un serpent de bronze sur un poteau. De la même manière, le Fils de l’homme doit être élevé, \v 15 pour que quiconque croit puisse avoir la vie éternelle en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : la vie du monde à venir, qui commence dès maintenant.

sw.L: Na sawasawa na Musa alivyomwinua nyoka nyikani, ndivyo inavyompasa Mwana wa Adamu kuinuliwa, \v 15 ili kila anayeamini apate uzima wa milele ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Musa alimwinua nyoka nyikani, na vivyo hivyo Mwana wa Adamu lazima ainuliwe, \v 15 ili kila anayeamini awe na uzima wa milele ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Zamani za kale huko jangwani, Musa alimwinua nyoka wa shaba juu ya mti. Vivyo hivyo, Mwana wa Adamu lazima ainuliwe, \v 15 ili kila anayeamini apate uzima wa milele ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: uzima wa nyakati zijazo, unaoanza sasa.

vi.L: Và như Môi-se đã giương cao con rắn trong hoang mạc, thì Con Người cũng phải được giương cao như vậy, \v 15 để mọi người tin đều ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà có sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Như Môi-se đã giương cao con rắn trong hoang mạc, Con Người cũng phải được giương cao như vậy, \v 15 để hễ ai tin đều có sự sống đời đời trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngày xưa, trong hoang mạc, Môi-se đã giương cao một con rắn bằng đồng trên một cây sào. Cũng vậy, Con Người phải được giương cao, \v 15 để mọi người tin đều có thể có sự sống đời đời trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: đó là sự sống của đời sắp đến, bắt đầu ngay từ bây giờ.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 광야에서 뱀을 높이 든 것처럼, 그와 같이 인자도 높이 들려야 한다. \v 15 그것은 믿는 사람마다 그 안에서 영원한 생명을 가지게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 모세가 광야에서 뱀을 높이 들어 올렸듯이, 인자도 그렇게 높이 들려야 한다. \v 15 믿는 사람은 누구나 그 안에서 영원한 생명을 얻게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 오래전에 광야에서 모세는 구리로 만든 뱀을 장대 위에 높이 매달았다. 그와 같이 인자도 높이 들려야 한다. \v 15 그래서 믿는 사람은 누구나 그 안에서 영원한 생명을 얻게 될 것이다. 영원한 생명은 다가올 세상의 생명인데, 지금부터 시작된다.

pt.L: E, assim como Moisés elevou a serpente no deserto, assim é necessário que o Filho do Homem seja elevado, \v 15 para que todo aquele que crê tenha {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} vida eterna.
pt.B: Moisés elevou a serpente no deserto, e do mesmo modo o Filho do Homem precisa ser elevado, \v 15 para que todo aquele que crê tenha a vida eterna {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.R: Muito tempo atrás, no deserto, Moisés elevou uma cobra de bronze num poste. Do mesmo modo, o Filho do Homem precisa ser elevado, \v 15 para que todo aquele que acredita tenha a vida eterna {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}: a vida do mundo que virá, que já começa agora.

decisions.choice: the bronze serpent of Numbers 21:8-9
decisions.reason: When poisonous snakes struck the people in the wilderness, God told Moses to make a serpent and set it on a pole; Moses made it of bronze, and anyone who had been bitten and looked at it lived (Numbers 21:4-9). As looking at the lifted serpent brought life, so believing in the lifted-up Son of Man brings eternal life.

decisions.choice: lifted up: raised on the cross, and by that exalted
decisions.reason: ὑψωθῆναι is used of raising something high and of exalting someone. John says plainly that it points to the way Jesus would die (12:32-33), and 8:28 and 12:34 use it the same way. In the Greek of Isaiah 52:13 the LORD's servant "will be lifted up and glorified". The cross is where Jesus is raised up and where he is glorified, so every level keeps "lifted up" with both senses.

decisions.choice: must: what God's purpose requires
decisions.reason: As in 3:7 and 3:30. The lifting up is not an accident but part of God's plan.

decisions.choice: in him goes with "have eternal life": eternal life is found in him
alternatives: in him goes with "believes": everyone who believes in him
decisions.reason: Elsewhere John always writes "believe in" with a different preposition (3:16, 18, 36), never with this one. So "in him" most likely goes with "may have eternal life": the life is in him (1:4; 20:31; 1 John 5:11). But the words stand right after "believes", and some read "believes in him". The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: everyone who believes may have eternal life in him (SBLGNT)
alternatives: everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "should not perish, but" from verse 16, and some change the preposition to the usual one for "believe in". The shorter text has the oldest witnesses. A reviewer should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, God's own life, which begins now
decisions.reason: Key term. The word for eternal belongs to "the age" to come; John stresses that believers have this life already (3:36; 5:24) and defines it as knowing God and Jesus Christ whom he sent (17:3).

decisions.choice: Long ago ... a bronze snake on a pole
decisions.reason: Readable says what the serpent was and how it was lifted up (Numbers 21:9), which readers need to follow the comparison.

decisions.choice: lifted up, with no "on the cross"
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John keeps "lifted up" at every level. Readable could add "on a cross", but that would lose the exaltation; the comparison with the snake on a pole already makes the picture clear.

decisions.choice: Moses lifted up ..., and in the same way
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the comparison but states the first half as a plain sentence.

decisions.choice: who believes may in him have eternal life
alternatives: who believes in him may have eternal life
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order and shows that "in him" goes with having life (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: the life of the age to come, which begins now
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John lets Readable explain eternal life once in a passage (meaning decision m6).

decisions.choice: serpent (B); snake (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the older word used in the story of Numbers 21; Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: levantado en alto, with no "en la cruz"
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice keeps "lifted up" at every level, with both senses: raised on the cross and exalted (meaning decision m2). "En alto" is part of the Greek verb, which comes from the word for height, and it keeps this verb apart from "levantar" in 2:19-22, which translates a different verb ("raise"). "Exaltado" would lose the cross.

decisions.choice: tenga en él vida eterna
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the Greek order, which shows that "en él" goes with having life (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: una serpiente de bronce sobre un poste
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what the serpent was and how it was lifted up (Numbers 21:9).

decisions.choice: la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage (meaning decision m6).

decisions.choice: élever, élevé at every level, with no "sur la croix"
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John (meaning decision m2). French "élever" means both to raise something high and to raise someone in honour ("élever au premier rang"), so one verb keeps the double sense of the Greek; "exalter" would keep only the honour, "hisser" only the lifting. Readable, like the English, lets the snake on a pole make the picture clear without adding "on the cross".

decisions.choice: la vie du monde à venir, qui commence dès maintenant
alternatives: la vie de l'âge à venir
decisions.reason: The book-wide explanation of eternal life, given once in this passage (meaning decision m6). "Le monde à venir" is the usual French phrase for the age to come; "l'âge à venir" sounds technical.

decisions.choice: kuinuliwa, with no "msalabani"
decisions.reason: "Kuinuliwa" means both to be lifted up and to be raised to honour, so it carries the double sense of the meaning note, as "lifted up" does in English. Adding "msalabani" (on the cross) would lose the second sense; "kutukuzwa" (be glorified) would lose the first.

decisions.choice: "giương cao" for lifted up
decisions.reason: "Giương cao" is to raise high for all to see, as a banner, and also carries honor, so it keeps both senses the meaning decision finds: raised on the cross and exalted. "Treo lên" (hang up) would say only the first.

decisions.choice: "높이 들리다"
decisions.reason: "높이" (high) lets the Korean carry both senses of the Greek: lifted up on the cross, and exalted. Naming the cross would keep only one.

decisions.choice: "영원한 생명" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "영생" is the familiar contraction, but "영원한 생명" keeps "생명", the word for life used throughout John, and is clearer to new readers.

decisions.choice: elevar (Moses and the Son of Man alike, every level)
decisions.reason: Following docs/john-terms.md, every level keeps one verb for both senses of meaning decision m2: "elevar" is to raise up and to raise in honour, where "levantar" says only the physical raising and "exaltar" only the honour. Moses "elevou" the serpent with the same verb, so the comparison stays visible. For the whole book (8:28; 12:32-34; 18:32).

decisions.choice: a vida eterna (every level); Readable explains it once: "a vida do mundo que virá, que já começa agora"
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6; docs/john-terms.md): the key term is "a vida eterna" at every level, and Readable explains it once in a passage, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m6).

source.text: Οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον ὥστε τὸν υἱὸν τὸν μονογενῆ ἔδωκεν, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν μὴ ἀπόληται ἀλλὰ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: Thus for loved the God the world, so that the Son the only [one] he gave, so that everyone the [one] believing in him not may perish but may have life eternal.

en.L: For in this way God loved the world, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the Son, the one and only, in order that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} may not perish but may have eternal life.
en.B: For God's love for the world was such that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} one and only Son, so that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} may not perish but have eternal life.
en.R: God loved the people of the world, and this is how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved them: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} one and only Son, so that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will not be lost but will have eternal life.

es.L: Porque así amó Dios al mundo: que dio al Hijo unigénito, para que todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no perezca, sino que tenga vida eterna.
es.B: Porque Dios amó al mundo de tal manera que dio a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo único, para que todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no perezca, sino que tenga vida eterna.
es.R: Dios amó a la gente del mundo, y así es como la amó: dio a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo único, para que todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no se pierda, sino que tenga vida eterna.

fr.L: Car c’est ainsi que Dieu a aimé le monde : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné le Fils, l’unique, afin que quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne se perde pas, mais ait la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Car tel a été l’amour de Dieu pour le monde qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils unique, pour que quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne périsse pas, mais possède la vie éternelle.
fr.R: Dieu a aimé les gens du monde, et voici comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a aimés : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils unique, pour que tous ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne soient pas perdus, mais aient la vie éternelle.

sw.L: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo Mungu alivyoupenda ulimwengu, kwamba alimtoa Mwana, yule wa pekee, ili kila anayemwamini asiangamie bali awe na uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu aliupenda ulimwengu kiasi kwamba alimtoa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa pekee, ili kila anayemwamini asiangamie, bali apate uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Mungu aliwapenda watu wa ulimwengu, na hivi ndivyo alivyowapenda: alimtoa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa pekee, ili kila anayemwamini asipotee, bali awe na uzima wa milele.

vi.L: Vì Đức Chúa Trời đã yêu thương thế gian như thế này: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban Con, Con duy nhất, để mọi người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không bị hư mất nhưng có sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Vì tình yêu của Đức Chúa Trời đối với thế gian là như thế này: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban Con một của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để mọi người tin vào Con ấy sẽ không bị hư mất nhưng được sự sống đời đời.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời yêu thương mọi người trong thế gian, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu họ như thế này: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban Con một của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để ai tin vào Con ấy sẽ không bị lạc mất, nhưng có sự sống đời đời.

ko.L: 하나님께서는 세상을 이렇게 사랑하셨다. 곧 그 아들, 하나뿐인 아들을 주셨다. 이는 그를 믿는 사람마다 멸망하지 않고 영원한 생명을 가지게 하시려는 것이다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 이렇게 세상을 사랑하셨다. 하나뿐인 아들을 내주신 것이다. 그것은 그 아들을 믿는 사람은 누구나 멸망하지 않고 영원한 생명을 얻게 하시려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 세상 사람들을 사랑하셨다. 그 사랑은 이런 것이었다. 하나님께서는 하나뿐인 아들을 주셨다. 그래서 그 아들을 믿는 사람은 누구나 망하지 않고 영원한 생명을 얻게 된다.

pt.L: Pois Deus amou o mundo deste modo: {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu o Filho, o único, para que todo aquele que crê {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} não pereça, mas tenha a vida eterna.
pt.B: Pois o amor de Deus pelo mundo foi tal que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho único, para que todo aquele que crê {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} não pereça, mas tenha a vida eterna.
pt.R: Deus amou as pessoas do mundo, e foi assim que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} as amou: {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho único, para que todo aquele que acredita {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} não se perca, mas tenha a vida eterna.

decisions.choice: Jesus's words to Nicodemus continue to the end of 3:21
alternatives: Jesus's words end at 3:15, and 3:16-21 is the evangelist's own reflection
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no quotation marks, so where the quotation ends is a judgment. Nothing in the text marks a break: 3:16 begins with "For", which ties it to 3:14-15, and the themes run on (the Son, believing, eternal life). On the other side, the verbs move to the past ("loved", "gave"), Nicodemus is not addressed again, and "the one and only Son" and "believe in the name" are the evangelist's own phrases elsewhere (1:12, 14, 18; 1 John 4:9). Every level keeps the quotation open to 3:21; the footnote gives the other view. 3:31-36 raises the same question.

decisions.choice: in this way: God's love took the form of giving the Son
alternatives: so much: God loved the world to such a degree
decisions.reason: Οὕτως normally means "thus, in this way" in John (3:8; 4:6; 21:1), and it has just been used in 3:14: "so must the Son of Man be lifted up". "For" links the two: this is how God loved the world, by giving the Son to be lifted up. ὥστε with the past tense states what actually happened: he gave. 1 John 4:9 makes the same point: "in this the love of God was revealed, that God sent his one and only Son." The other side: the greatness of the love is plain from what it gave, and the familiar "so loved" is often heard as "loved so much".

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, which has turned from God
decisions.reason: Key term. As in 1:10 and 1:29, the world here is humanity as a whole, which did not know its maker (1:10) and loves darkness (3:19). That God loves this world is the surprise.

decisions.choice: one and only, unique
decisions.reason: As in 1:14 and 1:18: μονογενής means unique, the only one of his kind, not "begotten" (see meaning decision m4 at 1:14). The footnote gives the familiar "only begotten".

decisions.choice: possibly an echo of Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 22)
decisions.reason: God told Abraham, "Take your son, your only son, whom you love" (Genesis 22:2), and praised him for not holding back his son (22:12, 16). Here God himself gives his one and only Son. John does not draw the link, so it is uncertain.

decisions.choice: gave: sent into the world and gave up to death
decisions.reason: The next verse says God "sent" the Son; 3:14 has just spoken of his lifting up. The giving includes both (compare Romans 8:32; Galatians 1:4).

decisions.choice: perish: be lost, destroyed, the opposite of eternal life
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of being lost (6:39; 10:28; 17:12). Believers still die (11:25); what they are spared is final ruin.

decisions.choice: "the Son" (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "his"; some of the oldest do not. The meaning is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in this way God loved the world, that (L); God's love for the world was such that (B)
alternatives: God so loved the world that
God loved the world so much that
decisions.reason: Literal gives the sense of the adverb (meaning decision m2). In Balanced, "such" can mean "of this kind" or "so great", which keeps the open question in meaning decision m2 without leaning to degree, as "so much" does. It departs from the familiar "so loved".

decisions.choice: his one and only Son
decisions.reason: English needs a possessive here; the Son is God's. Literal keeps "the Son".

decisions.choice: the people of the world ... this is how he loved them
alternatives: God loved the world in this way
decisions.reason: Readable says who the world is (meaning decision m3) and spells out "in this way".

decisions.choice: be lost
decisions.reason: "Perish" is an uncommon word for young readers; "be lost" is how John uses the verb elsewhere (meaning decision m7).

decisions.choice: everyone who believes, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Greek is general and the wording is already inclusive; no pronoun for the believer is needed, so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: así amó Dios al mundo: que dio (L); amó al mundo de tal manera que (B)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the sense of the adverb, "in this way" (meaning decision m2). In Balanced, "de tal manera" can mean "in such a way" or "so much", which keeps the open question in m2 without leaning to degree, as "tanto amó" would.
